target_customer: Small independent businesses in Latin America (initially beauty retailers buying wholesale; later small businesses building online stores)
problem: Independent LatAm retailers had to travel or wait days to restock and were limited to suppliers near them; later positioning was an easy no-code online store builder ('Shopify for LatAm').
business_model: Wholesale marketplace with supplier credit (2021), later SaaS e-commerce store builder
product_category: LatAm B2B wholesale marketplace / e-commerce platform

founders.name: Pedro Virgüez
founders.background_notes: Listed by Forbes Colombia (2021) but not on the current YC page.

founders.name: Alex Hakim
prior_employers: Early e-scooter startup in Colombia (VP Business Development)

founders.name: Tahi Hakim
prior_employers: Early e-scooter startup in Colombia (VP Finance)

technical_complexity.rationale: A wholesale ordering marketplace and store-builder are standard web/app engineering; operations (supplier onboarding, 30-day credit) were harder than the software.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of network effects or lock-in at 226 registered businesses and 30 suppliers; supplier relationships and credit were the only possible edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Shopify and Tiendanube were named by Forbes Colombia (Dec 2021) as the LatAm store-builder incumbents. They did not buy Preki; a startup peer, Sumer, acquired it in September 2023 for an undisclosed price, with Preki's brand to be phased out.

market_need_then: In March 2021 Preki reported 226+ registered businesses, 30 suppliers and 1,000+ products sold in 18 municipalities, targeting 3,500 businesses and $1M volume by year end, which suggests early but small demand for wholesale restocking.

branding.domain_note: Used preki.com; domain history not found. The site did not resolve from this environment.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand itself; Sumer's CTO said the Preki brand would eventually be phased out after the acquisition.

pivots.from: Wholesale marketplace with supplier credit for independent businesses, starting with beauty (Forbes, March 2021)
pivots.to: No-code e-commerce store builder 'Shopify for LatAm' (YC directory, later; Sumer called Preki a similar platform to its own in 2023)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; date unknown

outcome_analysis: Preki began as a wholesale marketplace with credit for LatAm retailers and later presented itself as Shopify for LatAm. Funding found is only the roughly $125,000 YC deal, and the company was bought by Sumer in September 2023 for an undisclosed price, mainly for its Brazil user base, with founders staying only as advisors and the brand to be retired. Whether this was a rescue or a modest win is not public, so no success or failure factors are asserted.
notes: Seedtable lists a ~$125K seed in March 2021 with True Capital and Pareto Holdings and CB Insights ~$130K total; aggregators only, so other investors are unverified. Founder lists conflict across sources (YC three names; Forbes four incl. Pedro Virguez; CB Insights lists Yerson Cacua, who is a Sumer founder, so likely an error). No competitor sources dated near W21 exist; Forbes 2021 named none. Pivot date unknown. The preki.com site failed DNS from this environment. Web Archive skipped.
